messages:
alice-support: Heads up — getting a cluster of customer tickets where streaming hosted API calls return 502s immediately. Started ~2026-03-19T09:20Z after the tracing rollout. Example: req_id=client-7f9a, customer saw instant 502 and no model response.
tracebot: deploy/edge-trace-injector v2.4 rolled to eu1/us-west at 2026-03-19T09:15Z (auto)
lee-sre: Can you paste the request id + client-side curl if available? Any pattern (long streams, big metadata)?
alice-support: Sample request from customer attached in ticket — they include a big JSON in X-Trace header (raw size ~65k). Quick curl they ran:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "X-Trace": "{...huge trace blob...}" \
  -d '@input.json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

maria-auth: auth service looks fine for those req_ids, no 5xx in auth logs. But I see a spike in incoming header sizes on the edge LB. nginx error on one edge node:

```
2026/03/19 09:21:03 [error] 23456#0: *9878 upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: _, request: "POST /v1/stream HTTP/2.0", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"
```

jordan-runtime: Envoy/edge proxies are logging 502 with upstream reset immediately after header processing. Tracing change injects big header into requests forwarded to internal services — some internal proxies (nginx sidecars) are hitting header buffer limits and closing the connection -> 502 back to client. I can repro locally by sending a large X-Trace header.

lee-sre: Repro steps (quick):
1) Hit hosted API streaming endpoint with a large X-Trace payload (>60k).
2) Observe immediate 502 and nginx error above.

jordan-runtime: Minimal repro curl sample:

```
python - <<PY
import requests
h = {'Authorization':'Bearer x', 'X-Trace': 'a'*65000}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', headers=h, data='{"prompt":"hi"}', timeout=10)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
PY
```

lee-sre: Possible mitigations:
- SHORT TERM: rollback trace injector rollout (stop injecting large trace payloads at edge) or strip/shorten the header in the edge before proxying.
- CONFIG: increase large_client_header_buffers / proxy_buffer_size on nginx sidecars and upstream proxies (but needs config rollout and careful canary).
- LONG TERM: switch to sending traces to collector via side channel (avoid stuffing large trace blobs into request headers).

maria-auth: I can push a temporary mitigation: nginx at ingress can drop X-Trace when above 8k and tag request with X-Trace-Dropped: true. That avoids the big header hitting internal services and should avoid 502s.

alice-support: Customer asked for ETA — can we do the drop now as an emergency config change? They have multiple users affected.

lee-sre: I'll coordinate a canary of the drop rule to one edge cluster now, monitor 1m error rate. If green, roll to remaining edges. Also opening a postmortem ticket and noting rollback of trace injector.

ben-customer: Thanks, appreciate quick triage. Biggest impact is live streaming sessions. Happy to test a fix if you need a customer-side probe.

jordan-runtime: Patch to the edge filter ready: `edge-filter: drop-large-trace-headers (v0.1)` — rolling to canary now. Will post results.

alice-support: :+1: tagging customer, will update ticket with mitigation and repro steps.

lee-sre: Update: canary in eu1 applied at 09:34Z, errors dropped from 6.2% -> 0.3% for streaming endpoint. Rolling to us-west now.

alice-support: ETA note sent to customer. Marking support escalation active -> will follow up in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
